title: Keep inserts ahead of part and merge debt
description: Model how client batching, partition fan-out, and merge capacity change part creation. The result teaches direction and operating signals rather than an exact MergeTree scheduler.

strategies.label: Chatty synchronous writes
strategies.detail: Each client sends tiny inserts directly. Request overhead and part creation stay visible to the application.

strategies.label: Bounded client batches
strategies.detail: The producer owns a bounded batch, retry identity, and flush deadline before sending one insert.

strategies.label: Asynchronous insert buffer
strategies.detail: The server groups small inserts before writing parts. Durability, acknowledgement, deduplication, and materialized-view behavior must match the selected settings and version.

notice: One insert can create more than one part when it touches multiple partitions. Actual merges are size-tiered and constrained by disks, codecs, mutations, replication, materialized views, TTL work, settings, and available background pools.
